briefing_2026-10-13_itcz_africa_latest: The Intertropical Front in the third dekad of September 2026 sat well north of its normal position over West Africa, near 21N at 15W and 19N between 10W and the Greenwich meridian against a normal of about 17.5N, and close to normal east of 10E at 14 to 15N. Compared with the previous dekad the front retreated south by 1 to 2 degrees between 5E and 30E while holding its position in the west. Dekadal rainfall of 100 to 200 mm fell along the Guinea coast and over Nigeria and Cameroon, with 50 to 100 mm across the Sahel belt, 25 to 75 mm over the Ethiopian highlands and mostly less than 10 mm over Kenya outside the west.
briefing_2026-10-13_kenya_ond_weekly_rai: Observed CHIRPS rainfall over the Kenya OND region stayed close to climatology at 2 to 3.5 mm per week from early August to mid September. The last two observed weeks, in late September and early October, each brought about 8 mm, against a climatology of roughly 4 and 6 mm. The season is therefore starting slightly ahead of normal, but the climatological ramp to 15 mm per week by mid October and a peak near 30 mm in early November is still to come.
briefing_2026-10-13_kenya_ond_weekly_sta: Weekly rainfall over the Kenya OND region was within half a standard deviation of normal from early August to mid September, with z-scores between -0.5 and +0.45. The week around 20 September stood out at about +2.1, and the most recent observed week was modestly above normal at about +0.3.
briefing_2026-10-13_kenya_ond_daily_rain: Daily CHIRPS rainfall averaged over the Kenya OND region stayed below 1 mm per day and close to climatology through August and the first half of September. A spike of about 5 mm per day occurred around 21 September, followed by days of 2.4 to 2.9 mm in late September and about 2.6 mm in early October, all above the climatological 1 to 1.5 mm per day for that time. Climatology rises to 4 to 5 mm per day in November, so the main season is still ahead.
briefing_2026-10-13_kenya_ond_last_week_: Observed CHIRPS rainfall for the week starting 29 September was light over most of the Kenya OND region, at 1 to 10 mm. The exception was the far east on the Somali border between about 2N and 3N, where 40 to 100 mm fell, with 20 to 50 mm in the far north across the Ethiopian border and isolated totals of 20 to 40 mm on the eastern slopes of the central highlands. The coast received 5 to 15 mm.
briefing_2026-10-13_kenya_week1_mae_vs_c: Week-1 rainfall errors against CHIRPS over Kenya grew through the four verifying weeks from 7 September to 4 October as the rains started. ECMWF ENS had the largest MAE in every week, rising from 5.0 to 15.8 mm per week, and KMSA downscaled went from the lowest error (1.7 mm) in the first week to 13.1 mm in the last. AIFS and GEFS were the most stable at 3 to 6 mm and had the lowest errors in the week of 28 September to 4 October (about 5 mm), while ECMWF ER reached 9.1 mm; Cumulus AI is only available for the first two weeks, at about 3 mm.
